payload.progression_strategy: Double progression within each exercise's rep range (per research.json finding for beginner fat-loss training: moderate rep ranges, 1-3 RIR, dumbbell loads capped around 20 kg). Week 1 starts one set lighter on 3-set exercises, weeks 2-7 run the prescribed sets while RIR tightens from 3 to 1-2, and week 8 is a lighter consolidation/deload. Once rep-range tops are reached, add load in small steps, or, when dumbbells cap out, add tempo, pauses, or shorter rest. Knee flexion stays shallow-to-moderate throughout. If you feel unusually fatigued or sore around weeks 4-5, take an easier week (drop to 2 sets per exercise at about 3 RIR) before continuing.

exercises.load_guidance: Choose a dumbbell you can lift for the bottom of the rep range with the target RIR. Double progression: once you hit the top of the range on all sets for 2 consecutive sessions with good form, increase load ~2.5-5% (smallest jump available; dumbbells are capped at about 20 kg, so when the cap is reached add reps, slow the 3-sec lowering, or shorten rest instead). Weeks 1-2: learn the movement and stay at the lower end of the range.

Choose a dumbbell you can lift for the bottom of the rep range with the target RIR. Double progression: once you hit the top of the range on all sets for 2 consecutive sessions with good form, increase load ~2.5-5% (smallest jump available; dumbbells are capped at about 20 kg, so when the cap is reached add reps, slow the 3-sec lowering, or shorten rest instead). Weeks 1-2: learn the movement and stay at the lower end of the range.

Bodyweight: progress by adding reps up to the top of the range, then slow the lowering (3 sec) or pause 1 sec at the hardest point, or move to a harder variation only when form stays clean. Weeks 1-2: learn the movement and stay at the lower end of the range. Keep knee bend shallow-to-moderate (box-limited, pain-free); stop if knee pain appears.
